quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane lets the car driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind can make it hard to use a side mirror.
Drivers should never use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, it is better to ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as other vehicles' horns. You can use your horn when needed, but do not depend on it to stay safe.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while you are stopping on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: To be seen more easily by other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Wearing bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: In areas where dangers could be present, a rider should:

options.text: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to be ready to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to be ready to stop quickly.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Keep your hand near the clutch and both brake levers. This helps you react faster in an emergency.

questions.question: The front brake supplies about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. To handle a passenger safely, slow down earlier when stopping and look for larger traffic gaps when crossing or merging.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally be:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space to be safe. Use a single-file line when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like any other vehicle. Mirrors alone are not enough to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard for other drivers to see your turn signals, you should:

options.text: Keep using your mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to warn drivers of your turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Riding directly beside another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Good because it blocks the wind.
Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside cars or trucks. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane without knowing you are there.

questions.question: You should use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch when:

options.text: Your throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If your throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, immediately use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch. This removes power from the rear wheel until you can safely stop.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash, keeps you comfortable, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear clothing with reflective material even during the day to help other drivers see you. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be regularly checked by riders.
Do not exist if your motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be regularly checked by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular routine.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Be ready to act to avoid a hazard.
Turn off your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your headlight during the day.
questions.explanation: Always make sure other drivers can see you to reduce crash risk. Use your signals, brake light, and correct lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which of the following should NOT be part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you be seen and see others. It helps you avoid wind gusts, blind spots, and hazards. Your position should discourage sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What gives you the best chance of surviving a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality, properly fitted helmet is the single best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.
